A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TraDy research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on CNNs and transformers, including accuracy results in Tables 1–5, gradient-distribution studies, efficiency measurements, and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports Velocity baseline accuracy and efficiency results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same offline layer selection and uniform channel resampling between epochs under a memory budget. The RGN metric and top-K selection procedure are unchanged; proposed transformer refinements remain future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet pretraining, the same seven vision datasets, and QNLI, RTE, and SST2. Transformer experiments and absolute versus proportional memory-budget scenarios already appear in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: V2 adds Quélennec et al.'s Velocity as an evaluated CNN comparator in Table 1 and Figures 4–5. SU and the existing static and dynamic selection controls remain. PaCA is linked conceptually to the existing S-Full Random baseline, without a separately reported evaluation.

E3.justification: The new Velocity comparison uses only the weight component of the memory budget, excluding activation memory, as specified in v2 Appendix D.1. Existing training schedules, budgets, metrics, and transformer evaluation regimes are retained. The explicit SGD/no-momentum statement is newly disclosed implementation information.

E4.justification: The MobileNetV2/Food efficiency case study is extended to Velocity, examining the activation-storage and computational costs of neuron-level selection through epoch-wise traces in v2 Figure 5. Existing RGN-thresholding, layer-contribution, and top-K sensitivity analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds, means with standard deviations, and the same correlation and t-test procedures. Velocity adds results using these existing reporting practices; no increased run count or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: V2 adds Velocity accuracy rows, pairwise comparison cells, and efficiency traces. For example, Table 1 newly reports a Velocity average of 76.15±0.70 for MobileNetV2-w0.35 at listed budget 93,696. All retained numerical entries in Tables 1–5 match, allowing for equivalent formatting. These are added comparator results, not improved TraDy scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Propositions 3.1–3.2, and Equations 1–14 are retained. The layer-ranking derivation moves from Appendix B to Appendix C without substantive changes to its assumptions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning heavy-tailed gradients, architecture-dependent layer importance, task-dependent channel importance, and dynamic sampling. The headline 99% activation sparsity, 95% weight-derivative sparsity, and 97% FLOP reduction claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for Velocity's activation-memory and computational costs, discusses adapter methods' applicability under extreme memory constraints, and expands transformer limitations concerning layer selection and Fisher-information warm-up. Existing hardware-validation and total-backpropagation-cost limitations remain. Appendix A also retains the now-inconsistent statement that comparisons focus only on SU.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly specifies SGD without momentum and explains the memory rationale. Code and training-metric links change from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. Existing hardware, framework, schedules, and reproduction-instruction descriptions are retained; the PDFs do not establish changes to repository contents.

R1.justification: New Appendix B positions TraDy relative to LoRA, DoRA, and PaCA, including the asserted correspondence between PaCA and S-Full Random. The transformer discussion additionally cites He et al.'s sparse-matrix fine-tuning work. The original related-work discussion is otherwise substantially retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains intact. V2 moves experimental setup into Appendix D.1, reorganizes appendix sections, adds focused PEFT and transformer discussions, and introduces acknowledgements. Citations change from numbered to author–year style, alongside limited wording and affiliation edits.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR layout and substantially rearranges displays: CNN heatmaps are split between the main text and appendix, several horizontal figure panels become vertical arrangements, and transformer tables are embedded beside prose. Table 1 and the comparison plots gain Velocity entries; the efficiency plot adds a broken activation-sparsity axis.

improvement.justification: The Velocity experiments partly address v1's missing comparison with a prior dynamic selection method, while explicit optimizer information improves reproducibility. These gains are limited by different memory accounting for Velocity, the stale SU-only limitation, and PEFT superiority argued indirectly rather than experimentally demonstrated. The core method, theory, and retained results are unchanged.
